'''Arven Wendik''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] who served in [[Bravo Squadron/Legends|Bravo Flight]] as [[Bravo Three]] under the [[Royal Naboo Security Forces/Legends|Royal Naboo Security Forces]] during the waning [[Standard year/Legends|years]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. In [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], he participated in the [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|Battle of Naboo]].

==Biography==
{{Quote|Did I mention I used to be a pilot? I flew in the Battle of Naboo years ago. I miss flying sometimes, but the work I do here is valuable. I'm thinking of the old days because Imperial fighters have just shot down an Alliance pilot. I hope he bailed out in time. Will you go look for him?|Captain Arven Wendik|<ref name="SWG:AED">{{GalaxiesAED}}</ref>}}
[[File:ArvenGCW.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Captain Arven Wendik in Dee'ja Peak during the time of the Galactic Civil War]]
A [[Human/Legends|Human]], Arven Wendik joined the [[Royal Naboo Security Forces/Legends|Royal Naboo Security Forces]] and served as a [[Lieutenant/Legends|Lieutenant]] in [[Bravo Squadron/Legends|Bravo Flight]] in the years prior to and during the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]].

Arven Wendik was an expert in [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ship]] capabilities, and many anti-warship tactical strategies were credited to him. In [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], he flew as [[Bravo Three]] during the [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|battle]] against the [[Vuutun Palaa/Legends|Droid Control Ship]] in orbit over [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]], and survived the battle. During the battle, he flew the [[N-1 starfighter/Legends|N-1 starfighter]] ''[[Bravo 3/Legends|Bravo 3]]''.

During the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], sometime following the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]] in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], Wendik stayed at the [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Dee'ja Peak/Legends|Dee'ja Peak]] on Naboo. By then, he was a member of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] and held the rank of [[Captain/Legends|captain]].
{{GameMechanics|legends=1}}
During his stay in Dee'ja Peak, Wendik employed the help of a [[Spacer/Legends|spacer]] affiliated with the Rebellion to deliver forged [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] permits to the female [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] [[Alowi Fintz]]. Fintz, a well-paid friend of the Alliance, needed the forged permits in order to ship medical supplies off Naboo, and deliver them to where they were needed. Although Fintz lamented not getting paid on time by the Rebellion, and was fearful that the permits would not pass Imperial scrutiny, she nonetheless accepted the documents from the Rebel courier so that the medical supplies could be delivered. With the contract complete, Wendik paid the spacer twenty-five [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]], and asked the individual to speak with him again soon. Wendik soon learned that Imperial [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]] shot down a [[Rebel pilot/Legends|Rebel pilot]] over Naboo. As a seasoned [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] himself, Wendik was affected by the news and reminisced of his days in Bravo Flight and the Battle of Naboo. Eager to save the pilot, a man named [[Grel Rommo]], Wendik asked his Rebel agent to locate Rommo, and bring him back safely. In the meantime, Wendik would make arrangements to send the pilot offworld. The agent obliged, but was attacked by three Imperial [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] looking for the downed pilot during a patrol. Nonetheless, the Rebel had the upper hand, and [[Death/Legends|killed]] the three Imperials. Rommo, who had bailed out of his starfighter, was located soon afterwards by the Rebel, and escorted safely back to the city. For completing the daring operation, Wendik awarded the Rebel-aligned spacer fifty credits.

Although he was grateful, Wendik had further assignments for the Rebel agent. In a worrisome turn of events, Wendik discovered that one of his informants, a female individual named [[Needia Solum]], was captured by the Empire on her way to Dee'ja Peak. The Imperials were then in the process of delivering her to Imperial [[High Inquisitor]] [[Mal Sikander]] for questioning. Wendik was certain that the [[Inquisitorius/Legends|Inquisitor]] would make her talk, compromising the Alliance's cover in Dee'ja Peak. In the meantime, intelligence reports concluded that she was being held by several stormtroopers and an [[Officer/Legends|officer]]. Captain Wendik knew that a rescue operation would be extremely dangerous, so he informed his Rebel agent to form a small but skilled strike team. Grasping the severity of the situation, the agent agreed, and embarked on a mission with a strike team to secure the Rebel informant. Despite the danger, Solum was rescued, and her captors, a [[Warrant Officer/Legends|Warrant Officer]] and three stormtroopers, were killed. With Solum safely back in Dee'ja Peak, Wendik paid out seventy-five credits.

It was later discovered that the Empire had set up a listening post in the wilderness to track the Rebels' ships as they landed nearby. Wendik was eager to have the listening post blasted to pieces. The Rebel agent thought Wendik was out of his mind to propose such a mission. Yet Wendik assured the individual that it was only a listening post, not a stormtrooper [[Barracks/Legends|barracks]]. By Wendik's estimate, the post was staffed with three or four stormtroopers, and at least a couple [[Technician/Legends|technicians]]. A strike team would once again be required, but Wendik believed that the mission could be accomplished. For the last time, the loyal Rebel agreed to fulfill Wendik's contract. A strike team was assembled, and they set out towards the known location of the Imperial listening post.
{{Endgame}}

==Behind the scenes==
Arven Wendik was portrayed by [[Clarence Smith]] in [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''The Phantom Menace'']].

Wendik later appeared as a [[Wikipedia:Non-player character|non-player character]] in the [[2003]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] [[Star Wars Galaxies|''Star Wars Galaxies: An Empire Divided'']], a [[Wikipedia:Massively multiplayer online role-playing game|massively multiplayer online roleplaying game]] developed by [[Sony]] Online Entertainment and published by [[LucasArts]], prior to its closure on [[December 15]], [[2011]]. Players who performed a series of [[:w:c:swg:Quest|quests]] for Wendik, who now held the rank of [[W:c:swg:Captain|captain]], had to deliver forged permits to Alowi Fintz, and escort Grel Rommo and Needia Solum to [[W:c:swg:Dee'ja Peak|Dee'ja Peak]]. The final mission, which involved destroying an Imperial listening post, was impossible to complete, as no enemies spawned at the assigned [[W:c:swg:Waypoint|waypoint]]. The quests were eventually disabled by the developers as a result of this buggy mission. Nonetheless, Wendik remained standing in Dee'ja Peak. Although the player could choose not to do Wendik's quests, this article assumes 100% game completion, except in the case of the final mission, which could not be completed.

In the game, Wendik's appearance differed from that in ''The Phantom Menace''. The game depicted him with a lighter skin tone, and more [[Color/Legends|amber-like]] [[Eye/Legends|eyes]].
